subject: yellow-bellied sea snake
title: Surrounded by Ocean, This Snake Goes Six Months Without a Drink

scenes.text: This snake is surrounded by water, and dying of thirst.
The yellow-bellied sea snake lives its whole life drifting at sea.
It refuses seawater, even badly dehydrated. Its salt glands can't keep up.
Off Costa Rica, dry seasons last six or seven months. The snakes shrink by up to a quarter of their weight.
When storms hit, rainwater floats on top of the sea. The snakes rise and sip that thin fresh layer.
An ocean of water, and it has to wait for rain.

description:
The yellow-bellied sea snake spends its entire life at sea, yet it refuses to drink seawater even when dehydrated.
Off Guanacaste, Costa Rica, dry seasons last six or seven months and the snakes can lose up to 25% of their body mass; when it rains they surface to drink from the freshwater lens that floats on the ocean (Lillywhite, University of Florida, 2014). Its salt glands are too small to turn seawater into the water it needs.
What other animal lives somewhere that should be impossible?
first_comment: Losing a quarter of your body mass would kill a human. Which animal survives the harshest thirst?
